workflow.description: "steps" is this envelope's current wire vocabulary; a document using the legacy "nodes" key (every workflow export produced before this rename) is still accepted on import.

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: Atlas card change
stepTypes.Description: Fires when a card of the chosen kind is created or updated in Atlas (docs/adr/0038). Cycle guard: a run this trigger started never re-fires itself from a write it makes to its own source card, so a workflow that both reacts to and updates the same card can't loop.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: Which Atlas card kind to watch. Fires only for cards of this kind.

stepTypes.Output: the changed card's id -- also seeds cardId/kindId/cardTitle/changeType as typed Attributes when this workflow declares them

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: callable by another workflow
stepTypes.Description: Fires only when invoked as a child by another workflow's Child Workflow step (docs/adr/0010) -- never by a real external event, no listener process. Modeled on n8n's own "Execute Workflow Trigger": a workflow rooted in this trigger declares itself a valid child target, decoupled from whatever its trigger would otherwise be. The child-workflow picker only lists workflows rooted here -- one rooted in a real-event trigger (filesystem-watch, clipboard-watch, ...) can't be invoked this way, since a parent has no way to synthesize that event.

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: clipboard change
stepTypes.Description: Fires whenever the clipboard's content changes.

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: filesystem change
stepTypes.Description: Fires when a file or folder under the configured path is added, changed, or deleted.

ConfigFields.Label: Path to watch
ConfigFields.Description: Absolute path to a file or directory.

ConfigFields.Label: Filename pattern (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: A glob like *.md or report-*.csv -- only files whose name matches fire the trigger. Leave empty to fire on any change.

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: hotkey
stepTypes.Description: Fires on a global keyboard shortcut, even when Mill isn't focused. Bound via TriggerService, not a config field here -- pressing the combo is better UX than typing it.
stepTypes.Output: empty payload — the run starts here

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: manual
stepTypes.Description: Fires on-demand when a user clicks Run/Test. No listener process.
stepTypes.Output: empty payload — the run starts here

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: schedule
stepTypes.Description: Fires on a cron schedule.

ConfigFields.Label: Cron expression
ConfigFields.Description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday).

stepTypes.Output: empty payload — the run starts here

stepTypes.Label: Trigger: system event
stepTypes.Description: Fires when Mill's own execution engine emits an internal event -- docs/adr/0035, SPEC.md §3.4's Group D unparked. Mill dogfoods its own trigger/composition surface for platform-internal behavior (the forward-pending-approvals example workflow is the first real user) instead of a bespoke Go code path per event. Loop rule (docs/adr/0035 item 4, n8n's Error-Trigger precedent): a run whose OWN root trigger is trigger-system-event never emits a system event of its own, regardless of kind -- a chain always bottoms out after one hop, so this trigger can never fire itself into a cycle.

ConfigFields.Label: Event
ConfigFields.Description: Which internal event fires this trigger. "Decision parked" fires when a guardrail ask or human-review checkpoint parks awaiting approval; the other three fire once a run reaches a terminal state.

ConfigFields.Label: Workflow scope
ConfigFields.Description: Fire for every workflow's matching event, or scope to one specific workflow. Empty means all workflows.

stepTypes.Output: JSON payload: {event, runId, workflowId, workflowLabel, nodeId?, timestamp} -- the run/decision that caused this event. nodeId is only set for decision-parked (the parked step's ID); empty for run-completed/run-failed/run-cancelled.

stepTypes.Label: Capture: attribute value
stepTypes.Description: Replaces the payload with the value of one of this workflow's declared Attributes -- e.g. a callable workflow's typed input, or a value a Decision already routed on.

ConfigFields.Label: Attribute
ConfigFields.Description: The declared Attribute key to read (Configure > Attributes, or the typed input a calling workflow bound).

stepTypes.Label: Capture: clipboard HTML
stepTypes.Description: Reads the clipboard's HTML. If there's no HTML flavor (many apps only put plain text), falls back to the plain-text flavor rather than failing -- the capture fallback order docs/SPEC.md §5 names (try HTML, then plain text; DOM-read via the browser bridge is the third tier, not built yet).

stepTypes.Label: Capture: clipboard info
stepTypes.Description: Reads macOS's own "clipboard info" report (which flavors -- HTML, plain text, images, ... -- are currently on the pasteboard, and their byte sizes) and summarizes whether HTML and plain text are present, followed by the raw report. A diagnostic for the Confluence-style clipboard ambiguity docs/SPEC.md §5 names: whether HTML was actually on the clipboard, made directly inspectable instead of inferred from a capture succeeding or failing.
stepTypes.Output: a summary of the clipboard's flavors

stepTypes.Label: Capture: file
stepTypes.Description: Reads a local file into the payload. "payload" source treats the CURRENT payload as the file path (what a filesystem-watch trigger's changed-path output supplies, docs/SPEC.md §3.4); "literal" source reads a fixed path instead.

ConfigFields.Label: Path source
ConfigFields.Description: "payload" reads the path from the upstream payload (a filesystem-watch trigger's changed path); "literal" reads the fixed path below instead.

ConfigFields.Label: Path
ConfigFields.Description: The file path to read when "Path source" is literal. Ignored when source is payload.

stepTypes.Label: Run another workflow
stepTypes.Description: Runs another of your workflows as a step and uses its result as this workflow's payload. The other workflow must start with the "callable by another workflow" trigger (docs/adr/0010) -- that's what marks it as safe to be invoked from here rather than by a hotkey or schedule of its own.

ConfigFields.Label: Workflow
ConfigFields.Description: Which workflow to run. Only workflows whose trigger is "callable by another workflow" appear here -- if the list is empty, create a workflow and drag that trigger onto its canvas first.

ConfigFields.Label: Skip duplicate runs (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to run fresh every time (the normal case). To make repeated runs with the same input reuse the first run's recorded result instead of running again, put a value here that identifies the input -- a literal, or attr:<name> to use one of this workflow's attributes.

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always call the child's published version. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact snapshot, unaffected by later publishes.

ConfigFields.Label: Store result in attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Also write the child workflow's result into this workflow's named Attribute, so later steps (a Decision condition, another binding) can reference it as attr:<name>.

stepTypes.Label: Code: run command
stepTypes.Description: Runs one command locally, inside a Configure-authored ExecEnv (pinned shell/dir/env -- docs/SPEC.md §6, docs/adr/0026). External effect -- the ambient guardrail gate asks by default, same as integration-http/mcp-tool-call. Source "payload" runs the captured/upstream payload as the command (SPEC §2.1's paste-a-command loop); "literal" runs a fixed script instead. A running command can be stopped from this workflow's Runs tab (real process-group kill, not just marking the run failed) -- DBOS itself cannot interrupt an executing step (ADR-0026's Amendment), so Mill's own procexec supervises the live process directly.

ConfigFields.Label: Execution environment
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored environment (shell, working directory, env vars) this command runs inside.

ConfigFields.Label: Command source
ConfigFields.Description: "payload" runs the captured/upstream payload as the command; "literal" runs the script below instead.

ConfigFields.Label: Script
ConfigFields.Description: The command to run when "Command source" is literal. Ignored when source is payload.

ConfigFields.Label: Timeout (seconds)
ConfigFields.Description: Kills the command if it hasn't finished within this many seconds.

stepTypes.Output: combined stdout+stderr from the executed command

stepTypes.Label: Human review
stepTypes.Description: Pauses the run for a person: the item lands in the Review queue (and this workflow's Runs tab), where a reviewer can approve, deny, and fill in values for this workflow's declared Attributes -- their input flows into the resumed run. Denying (or 24 hours of silence) stops the run. A deliberate, visible checkpoint you drew into the flow -- the ambient guardrail rules (Configure > Guardrails) never skip it.

ConfigFields.Label: Message to the approver
ConfigFields.Description: Shown alongside the approval request, so future-you knows what this checkpoint is guarding.

ConfigFields.Label: Ask for these attributes
ConfigFields.Description: Comma-separated Attribute keys the reviewer should fill in. Leave empty to ask for all of the workflow's Attributes.

stepTypes.Label: Integration: HTTP call
stepTypes.Description: Calls a Configure-authored integration's API and replaces the payload with the response body. The step only picks WHICH integration and binds data -- method, endpoint path, and body all live on the integration itself (Configure > Integration): transport configuration belongs on the integration, not the workflow step. Legacy steps saved with their own path/method/bodyTemplate config keep working (those keys still win when present); they're just no longer authorable here.

ConfigFields.Label: Integration
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored integration this step calls.

stepTypes.Label: List: lookup
stepTypes.Description: Looks up an Attributes value in a Configure-authored List and writes the matched entry back into Attributes. listId is FieldText for the same reason integration-http's requestId is above -- Lists are runtime, Configure-authored data (the Inspector renders a live picker for it, RefKind, docs/adr/0009).

ConfigFields.Label: List ID
ConfigFields.Description: The ID of a list configured on the Configure page.

ConfigFields.Label: Input attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field's value to look up.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field the matched value gets written to.

ConfigFields.Label: If no match
ConfigFields.Description: What to do when the input value isn't in the list.

ConfigFields.Label: Default value
ConfigFields.Description: Written to the output attribute when there's no match and "If no match" is "default".

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always resolve this List's current rows. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact published snapshot, unaffected by later row edits.

stepTypes.Label: List: search
stepTypes.Description: Searches a Configure-authored List's rows against one or more match parameters (exact or fuzzy, per-column, AND'd together) and writes the result into Attributes. Supersedes list-lookup for anything beyond a single exact key match -- list-lookup keeps working unchanged for existing workflows. Expired rows are excluded by default (docs/goals/0011-lists-maturation.md's own researched default, uniform across exact and fuzzy matching); "Include expired rows" opts in.

ConfigFields.Label: List
ConfigFields.Description: The Configure-authored List to search.

ConfigFields.Label: Match parameters
ConfigFields.Description: JSON array of match criteria, ALL must match (AND): [{"column":"code","value":"attr:code","matchType":"exact"},{"column":"name","value":"Untied States","matchType":"fuzzy","threshold":0.7}]. value is a literal or "attr:<name>". Authored via the Inspector's match-parameter rows; this raw field stays the LLM-authoring vocabulary (docs/adr/0025).

ConfigFields.Label: Include expired rows
ConfigFields.Description: Off by default -- Expired rows never match unless explicitly included.

ConfigFields.Label: Stop at first match
ConfigFields.Description: Stops scanning after the first match. The output shape stays the same typed Object either way -- results just has at most one entry -- so turning this on or off never changes what a downstream Decision/binding can reference.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the typed search-result object.

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always resolve this List's current rows. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact published snapshot, unaffected by later row edits.

stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged; matches -> a typed Object attribute ({results, matched, first_match, match_count, list_id})

stepTypes.Label: MCP: tool call
stepTypes.Description: Calls one tool on a Configure-authored MCP server and replaces the payload with its text result (docs/SPEC.md §3.6). mcpServerId is FieldText for the same reason integration-http's requestId is -- runtime, Configure-authored data (the Inspector renders a live picker for it, RefKind, docs/adr/0009); toolName is picked from the server's live tool list in the canvas Inspector (MCPToolArgsEditor.tsx), falling back to typing the exact name when the server can't be reached.

ConfigFields.Label: MCP Server ID
ConfigFields.Description: The ID of an MCP server configured on the Configure page.

ConfigFields.Label: Tool name
ConfigFields.Description: The exact tool name, from that server's own tool list.

ConfigFields.Label: Arguments (JSON)
ConfigFields.Description: Optional JSON object of arguments to pass to the tool. Top-level string values of the form "attr:<name>" resolve to the named Attribute's typed value at run time (a number/boolean Attribute stays a JSON number/boolean, not stringified); every other value is sent as-is.

stepTypes.Label: AI: Classify
stepTypes.Description: Sends the running payload (plus an optional instruction) to a Configure-authored AI provider and asks it to pick exactly one of this step's own declared categories, writing the choice into a named Attribute -- a dedicated classification step (Dify's own precedent researched in docs/goals/0031-ai-node-family.md), not composed from extract-structured, since "pick one of these labels" is common enough across real workflows to deserve its own shape. Pairs with Branch: route on the written Attribute to act on the classification. The category list is this workflow's own business decision (step-local, not Configure-authored) -- two workflows classifying into different category sets is normal, not drift.

ConfigFields.Label: AI provider
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored AI provider (local Ollama or a BYO endpoint) this step calls.

ConfigFields.Label: Instruction
ConfigFields.Description: Optional guidance sent as the user message, followed by the current payload. Leave empty to classify the payload with no extra instruction.

ConfigFields.Label: Categories
ConfigFields.Description: One category per line -- the AI picks exactly one of these.

ConfigFields.Label: Write category to
ConfigFields.Description: The declared Attribute key the chosen category is written into.

stepTypes.Output: unchanged payload -- the chosen category is written into the named Attribute below

stepTypes.Label: AI: Completion
stepTypes.Description: Sends a prompt (plus the running payload) to a Configure-authored AI provider -- local Ollama, or a BYO OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic endpoint -- and replaces the payload with its text completion. Composition (docs/goals/0031-ai-node-family.md): the system prompt is this step's own System prompt field; the user message is Prompt followed by the current payload (blank-line separated) when the payload is non-empty, else Prompt alone. One deterministic call per run -- never a loop or autonomous agent behavior (docs/SPEC.md §1.1's locked invariant). A local (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1) provider runs without an approval ask; any other endpoint asks by default, the same posture integration-http already has for outbound calls.

ConfigFields.Label: AI provider
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored AI provider (local Ollama or a BYO endpoint) this step calls.

ConfigFields.Label: System prompt
ConfigFields.Description: Optional system-level instruction sent ahead of the user message. Leave empty for none.

ConfigFields.Label: Prompt
ConfigFields.Description: The instruction sent as the user message, followed by the current payload (if any).

stepTypes.Output: the AI completion text, replacing the payload

stepTypes.Label: AI: Extract structured data
stepTypes.Description: Sends a prompt (plus the running payload) to a Configure-authored AI provider, requests a JSON-schema-constrained structured response, and writes each declared output field into this workflow's Attributes by the same key -- the step that composes with Branch for real decisioning (docs/goals/0031-ai-node-family.md). Composition matches process-ai-completion: user content = Prompt + payload. Every declared field is required in the requested schema; a field the provider's response omits still appears in Attributes, zero-valued for its type.

ConfigFields.Label: AI provider
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored AI provider (local Ollama or a BYO endpoint) this step calls.

ConfigFields.Label: Prompt
ConfigFields.Description: The extraction instruction sent as the user message, followed by the current payload (if any).

ConfigFields.Label: Output fields
ConfigFields.Description: The typed fields this step extracts -- each becomes an Attribute of the same key, authored via the field editor below (not raw JSON).

stepTypes.Output: unchanged payload -- the extracted typed result is written into the named Attributes below

stepTypes.Label: Atlas: find cards
stepTypes.Description: Searches a Kind's cards in Atlas against one or more match parameters (exact or fuzzy, AND'd together) and writes the result into Attributes. Match against "title" or any of the Kind's own field keys.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: Which Atlas card kind to search.

ConfigFields.Label: Match parameters
ConfigFields.Description: JSON array of match criteria, ALL must match (AND): [{"column":"title","value":"attr:leadName","matchType":"exact"},{"column":"status","value":"New","matchType":"exact"}]. value is a literal or "attr:<name>".

ConfigFields.Label: Stop at first match
ConfigFields.Description: Stops scanning after the first match.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the typed search-result object.

stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged; matches -> a typed Object attribute ({results, matched, first_match, match_count})

stepTypes.Label: Process: extract HTML subtree
stepTypes.Description: Extracts one element (by CSS selector) out of the payload's HTML, dropping everything else -- e.g. a saved page's main-content region, stripping nav/header/footer chrome before converting to Markdown. Fails the step if nothing matches (fail-safe: never silently passes the whole, unfiltered document through).

ConfigFields.Label: CSS selector
ConfigFields.Description: A CSS selector, optionally comma-separated (e.g. "#main-content, main, article") -- the first matching element (in document order) is kept.

stepTypes.Label: Process: HTML → Markdown
stepTypes.Description: Converts HTML into Markdown, preserving structure (headings, bold, lists).

stepTypes.Label: Process: Inject text
stepTypes.Description: Prepends or appends configured static text to the payload -- e.g. a fixed hint or instruction pasted alongside a workflow's real output.

ConfigFields.Label: Text to inject
ConfigFields.Description: The literal text this step adds to the payload. Left empty, this step is a no-op.

ConfigFields.Label: Placement
ConfigFields.Description: Where the text goes relative to the existing payload.

stepTypes.Label: Process: Run receipt
stepTypes.Description: Renders this run's own recorded evidence -- its steps so far, their guardrail verdicts, and which Mill build ran them -- as a JSON receipt, replacing the payload. Only covers steps that ran BEFORE this one, since the run is still in flight when this step executes. Compose it with an Apply step (clipboard/file write) to hand the receipt to an external agent -- there is no separate send path.
stepTypes.Output: a JSON receipt of this run's steps so far

stepTypes.Label: Ruleset validation
stepTypes.Description: Validates the data flowing through this step against a set of named rules (business/data validation -- e.g. "amount below limit", "country allowed"). Every rule must pass for the payload to continue unchanged; any failing rule fails the run, naming exactly which rules failed. A rule that cannot evaluate counts as failed (fail-safe). Distinct from Decision (which routes) and from guardrail rules (which govern whether a step may execute at all).
stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged, if all rules pass

stepTypes.Label: Atlas: create card
stepTypes.Description: Creates a new card in Atlas of the chosen Kind. "Field values" binds the Kind's own declared fields, each a literal or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: Which Atlas card kind to create.

ConfigFields.Label: Title
ConfigFields.Description: The new card's title -- a literal or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Field values
ConfigFields.Description: JSON object mapping the Kind's field keys to a literal or attr:<name>, e.g. {"status":"New","owner":"attr:currentUser"}.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the new card's id, so a later step can reference it (e.g. to link it or update it further).

stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged; the new card's id -> the output attribute, if named

stepTypes.Label: Atlas: link cards
stepTypes.Description: Creates a typed relation between two existing Atlas cards. "From"/"To" are each a literal card id or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: From
ConfigFields.Description: The relation's source card -- a literal card id, or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: To
ConfigFields.Description: The relation's target card -- a literal card id, or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Relation
ConfigFields.Description: Which kind of relation this is.

ConfigFields.Label: Label (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: An optional note describing this specific relation.

stepTypes.Label: Atlas: update card
stepTypes.Description: Writes field values onto an existing Atlas card, resolved by "Card" (a literal card id or attr:<name> -- e.g. attr:cardId from a trigger-atlas-card event, or an earlier Atlas: find cards result). Only the fields named in "Field values" change; everything else on the card is untouched.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: The card's own Kind -- names which field keys "Field values" may bind.

ConfigFields.Label: Card
ConfigFields.Description: Which card to update -- a literal card id, or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Field values
ConfigFields.Description: JSON object mapping the Kind's field keys to a literal or attr:<name>, e.g. {"status":"Processed"}.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the updated card's id.

stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged; the updated card's id -> the output attribute, if named

stepTypes.Label: Atlas: create from reply items
stepTypes.Description: Creates Atlas records from an accepted clipboard reply's items: an item with a "title" becomes a card of its named kind, an item with "text" becomes a Scratchpad note. "Items" binds the attribute holding the accepted items as a JSON array.

ConfigFields.Label: Items attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field carries the accepted reply items (a JSON array).

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives a summary of what was created.

stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged; a created-summary JSON -> the output attribute, if named

stepTypes.Label: Apply: back up Mill data
stepTypes.Description: Takes a safe snapshot of your workflow history and settings, deleting older snapshots beyond how many you keep.

ConfigFields.Label: Snapshots to keep
ConfigFields.Description: How many recent backups to keep -- older ones are deleted automatically.

stepTypes.Label: Apply: write HTML to clipboard
stepTypes.Description: Writes configured HTML to the clipboard.

ConfigFields.Label: HTML to write
ConfigFields.Default:
Quarterly update

Here's a quick summary, with the important bit called out.

  • Runbook actions now support global keyboard shortcuts
  • Clipboard capture preserves real structure, not flattened text
  • The UI now runs on Primer, not hand-rolled CSS
ConfigFields.Description: The HTML content this step puts on the clipboard.

stepTypes.Label: Apply: write plain text to clipboard
stepTypes.Description: Writes the workflow's current payload to the clipboard as plain text.

stepTypes.Label: Apply: move file
stepTypes.Description: Moves or renames a local file to a new location.

ConfigFields.Label: Source file
ConfigFields.Description: File to move. Leave empty to use the incoming payload, or set a path or attr: value.

ConfigFields.Label: Destination
ConfigFields.Description: Where the file goes. Tokens: {filename} {name} {ext} {date:2006-01-02} {attr:key}. End with / to keep the file's name.

ConfigFields.Label: Create missing folders
ConfigFields.Description: Creates the destination's parent folders if they don't exist yet. Off fails the step instead when a folder is missing.

ConfigFields.Label: If the destination exists
ConfigFields.Description: Fail stops the step. Suffix adds " (2)", " (3)", and so on to the file name.

stepTypes.Label: Apply: write to file
stepTypes.Description: Writes the payload to a local file, appending to or overwriting its existing contents.

ConfigFields.Label: File path
ConfigFields.Description: Where to write. Use an absolute path, or start with ~ for your home folder.

ConfigFields.Label: Mode
ConfigFields.Description: Append adds to the end of the file. Overwrite replaces its entire contents.

ConfigFields.Label: Create missing folders
ConfigFields.Description: Creates the file's parent folders if they don't exist yet. Off fails the step instead when a folder is missing.

ConfigFields.Label: Timestamp
ConfigFields.Description: Append mode only: "datetime" puts a date-and-time line before each entry. Ignored in overwrite mode.

stepTypes.Label: List: apply row
stepTypes.Description: Creates or updates a row in a Configure-authored List: if an existing row's "Key column" value matches, only the fields named in "Field values" change (everything else on that row is untouched); otherwise a new row is appended. "Field values" binds the List's own declared column keys, each a literal or attr:<name> -- the same shape apply-atlas-card-create/update use.

ConfigFields.Label: List
ConfigFields.Description: The Configure-authored List to write to.

ConfigFields.Label: Key column
ConfigFields.Description: Which column identifies a row -- an existing row whose value in this column matches gets updated; no match appends a new row.

ConfigFields.Label: Field values
ConfigFields.Description: JSON object mapping the List's column keys to a literal or attr:<name>, e.g. {"task":"attr:taskName","status":"Done"}. Must include a value for the key column.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the row's id.

stepTypes.Output: payload unchanged; the row's id -> the output attribute, if named

stepTypes.Label: Branch: route
stepTypes.Description: Routes to one of several next steps based on a rule evaluated against this workflow's Attributes. A pure routing point -- its conditions live on its outgoing edges (SPEC.md §3.5), not here.
stepTypes.Output: payload and Attributes unchanged; routes to the matching outgoing edge

stepTypes.Label: Decision
stepTypes.Description: Ends the workflow with a Configure-authored, typed terminal outcome (docs/adr/0027): an outcome category (approve/deny/manual-review/action-needed/uncategorized) plus this Decision's own typed result fields. A manual-review Decision parks the run in the Review queue first -- approve continues to the outcome, deny/timeout fails closed, same mechanism the human-review step uses. A Decision with a configured webhook fires it (the same HTTPRequest execution path integration-http uses, with the outcome's typed outputs as the body) once the outcome is computed, and -- unlike a plain Decision -- asks for approval by default, exactly like integration-http does for the identical kind of outbound call.

ConfigFields.Label: Decision
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored Decision this terminal step reaches.

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always resolve this Decision's current definition. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact published snapshot, unaffected by later edits.

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: Atlas card change
nodeTypes.Description: Fires when a card of the chosen kind is created or updated in Atlas (docs/adr/0038). Cycle guard: a run this trigger started never re-fires itself from a write it makes to its own source card, so a workflow that both reacts to and updates the same card can't loop.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: Which Atlas card kind to watch. Fires only for cards of this kind.

nodeTypes.Output: the changed card's id -- also seeds cardId/kindId/cardTitle/changeType as typed Attributes when this workflow declares them

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: callable by another workflow
nodeTypes.Description: Fires only when invoked as a child by another workflow's Child Workflow step (docs/adr/0010) -- never by a real external event, no listener process. Modeled on n8n's own "Execute Workflow Trigger": a workflow rooted in this trigger declares itself a valid child target, decoupled from whatever its trigger would otherwise be. The child-workflow picker only lists workflows rooted here -- one rooted in a real-event trigger (filesystem-watch, clipboard-watch, ...) can't be invoked this way, since a parent has no way to synthesize that event.

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: clipboard change
nodeTypes.Description: Fires whenever the clipboard's content changes.

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: filesystem change
nodeTypes.Description: Fires when a file or folder under the configured path is added, changed, or deleted.

ConfigFields.Label: Path to watch
ConfigFields.Description: Absolute path to a file or directory.

ConfigFields.Label: Filename pattern (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: A glob like *.md or report-*.csv -- only files whose name matches fire the trigger. Leave empty to fire on any change.

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: hotkey
nodeTypes.Description: Fires on a global keyboard shortcut, even when Mill isn't focused. Bound via TriggerService, not a config field here -- pressing the combo is better UX than typing it.
nodeTypes.Output: empty payload — the run starts here

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: manual
nodeTypes.Description: Fires on-demand when a user clicks Run/Test. No listener process.
nodeTypes.Output: empty payload — the run starts here

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: schedule
nodeTypes.Description: Fires on a cron schedule.

ConfigFields.Label: Cron expression
ConfigFields.Description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday).

nodeTypes.Output: empty payload — the run starts here

nodeTypes.Label: Trigger: system event
nodeTypes.Description: Fires when Mill's own execution engine emits an internal event -- docs/adr/0035, SPEC.md §3.4's Group D unparked. Mill dogfoods its own trigger/composition surface for platform-internal behavior (the forward-pending-approvals example workflow is the first real user) instead of a bespoke Go code path per event. Loop rule (docs/adr/0035 item 4, n8n's Error-Trigger precedent): a run whose OWN root trigger is trigger-system-event never emits a system event of its own, regardless of kind -- a chain always bottoms out after one hop, so this trigger can never fire itself into a cycle.

ConfigFields.Label: Event
ConfigFields.Description: Which internal event fires this trigger. "Decision parked" fires when a guardrail ask or human-review checkpoint parks awaiting approval; the other three fire once a run reaches a terminal state.

ConfigFields.Label: Workflow scope
ConfigFields.Description: Fire for every workflow's matching event, or scope to one specific workflow. Empty means all workflows.

nodeTypes.Output: JSON payload: {event, runId, workflowId, workflowLabel, nodeId?, timestamp} -- the run/decision that caused this event. nodeId is only set for decision-parked (the parked step's ID); empty for run-completed/run-failed/run-cancelled.

nodeTypes.Label: Capture: attribute value
nodeTypes.Description: Replaces the payload with the value of one of this workflow's declared Attributes -- e.g. a callable workflow's typed input, or a value a Decision already routed on.

ConfigFields.Label: Attribute
ConfigFields.Description: The declared Attribute key to read (Configure > Attributes, or the typed input a calling workflow bound).

nodeTypes.Label: Capture: clipboard HTML
nodeTypes.Description: Reads the clipboard's HTML. If there's no HTML flavor (many apps only put plain text), falls back to the plain-text flavor rather than failing -- the capture fallback order docs/SPEC.md §5 names (try HTML, then plain text; DOM-read via the browser bridge is the third tier, not built yet).

nodeTypes.Label: Capture: clipboard info
nodeTypes.Description: Reads macOS's own "clipboard info" report (which flavors -- HTML, plain text, images, ... -- are currently on the pasteboard, and their byte sizes) and summarizes whether HTML and plain text are present, followed by the raw report. A diagnostic for the Confluence-style clipboard ambiguity docs/SPEC.md §5 names: whether HTML was actually on the clipboard, made directly inspectable instead of inferred from a capture succeeding or failing.
nodeTypes.Output: a summary of the clipboard's flavors

nodeTypes.Label: Capture: file
nodeTypes.Description: Reads a local file into the payload. "payload" source treats the CURRENT payload as the file path (what a filesystem-watch trigger's changed-path output supplies, docs/SPEC.md §3.4); "literal" source reads a fixed path instead.

ConfigFields.Label: Path source
ConfigFields.Description: "payload" reads the path from the upstream payload (a filesystem-watch trigger's changed path); "literal" reads the fixed path below instead.

ConfigFields.Label: Path
ConfigFields.Description: The file path to read when "Path source" is literal. Ignored when source is payload.

nodeTypes.Label: Run another workflow
nodeTypes.Description: Runs another of your workflows as a step and uses its result as this workflow's payload. The other workflow must start with the "callable by another workflow" trigger (docs/adr/0010) -- that's what marks it as safe to be invoked from here rather than by a hotkey or schedule of its own.

ConfigFields.Label: Workflow
ConfigFields.Description: Which workflow to run. Only workflows whose trigger is "callable by another workflow" appear here -- if the list is empty, create a workflow and drag that trigger onto its canvas first.

ConfigFields.Label: Skip duplicate runs (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to run fresh every time (the normal case). To make repeated runs with the same input reuse the first run's recorded result instead of running again, put a value here that identifies the input -- a literal, or attr:<name> to use one of this workflow's attributes.

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always call the child's published version. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact snapshot, unaffected by later publishes.

ConfigFields.Label: Store result in attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Also write the child workflow's result into this workflow's named Attribute, so later steps (a Decision condition, another binding) can reference it as attr:<name>.

nodeTypes.Label: Code: run command
nodeTypes.Description: Runs one command locally, inside a Configure-authored ExecEnv (pinned shell/dir/env -- docs/SPEC.md §6, docs/adr/0026). External effect -- the ambient guardrail gate asks by default, same as integration-http/mcp-tool-call. Source "payload" runs the captured/upstream payload as the command (SPEC §2.1's paste-a-command loop); "literal" runs a fixed script instead. A running command can be stopped from this workflow's Runs tab (real process-group kill, not just marking the run failed) -- DBOS itself cannot interrupt an executing step (ADR-0026's Amendment), so Mill's own procexec supervises the live process directly.

ConfigFields.Label: Execution environment
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored environment (shell, working directory, env vars) this command runs inside.

ConfigFields.Label: Command source
ConfigFields.Description: "payload" runs the captured/upstream payload as the command; "literal" runs the script below instead.

ConfigFields.Label: Script
ConfigFields.Description: The command to run when "Command source" is literal. Ignored when source is payload.

ConfigFields.Label: Timeout (seconds)
ConfigFields.Description: Kills the command if it hasn't finished within this many seconds.

nodeTypes.Output: combined stdout+stderr from the executed command

nodeTypes.Label: Human review
nodeTypes.Description: Pauses the run for a person: the item lands in the Review queue (and this workflow's Runs tab), where a reviewer can approve, deny, and fill in values for this workflow's declared Attributes -- their input flows into the resumed run. Denying (or 24 hours of silence) stops the run. A deliberate, visible checkpoint you drew into the flow -- the ambient guardrail rules (Configure > Guardrails) never skip it.

ConfigFields.Label: Message to the approver
ConfigFields.Description: Shown alongside the approval request, so future-you knows what this checkpoint is guarding.

ConfigFields.Label: Ask for these attributes
ConfigFields.Description: Comma-separated Attribute keys the reviewer should fill in. Leave empty to ask for all of the workflow's Attributes.

nodeTypes.Label: Integration: HTTP call
nodeTypes.Description: Calls a Configure-authored integration's API and replaces the payload with the response body. The step only picks WHICH integration and binds data -- method, endpoint path, and body all live on the integration itself (Configure > Integration): transport configuration belongs on the integration, not the workflow step. Legacy steps saved with their own path/method/bodyTemplate config keep working (those keys still win when present); they're just no longer authorable here.

ConfigFields.Label: Integration
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored integration this step calls.

nodeTypes.Label: List: lookup
nodeTypes.Description: Looks up an Attributes value in a Configure-authored List and writes the matched entry back into Attributes. listId is FieldText for the same reason integration-http's requestId is above -- Lists are runtime, Configure-authored data (the Inspector renders a live picker for it, RefKind, docs/adr/0009).

ConfigFields.Label: List ID
ConfigFields.Description: The ID of a list configured on the Configure page.

ConfigFields.Label: Input attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field's value to look up.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field the matched value gets written to.

ConfigFields.Label: If no match
ConfigFields.Description: What to do when the input value isn't in the list.

ConfigFields.Label: Default value
ConfigFields.Description: Written to the output attribute when there's no match and "If no match" is "default".

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always resolve this List's current rows. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact published snapshot, unaffected by later row edits.

nodeTypes.Label: List: search
nodeTypes.Description: Searches a Configure-authored List's rows against one or more match parameters (exact or fuzzy, per-column, AND'd together) and writes the result into Attributes. Supersedes list-lookup for anything beyond a single exact key match -- list-lookup keeps working unchanged for existing workflows. Expired rows are excluded by default (docs/goals/0011-lists-maturation.md's own researched default, uniform across exact and fuzzy matching); "Include expired rows" opts in.

ConfigFields.Label: List
ConfigFields.Description: The Configure-authored List to search.

ConfigFields.Label: Match parameters
ConfigFields.Description: JSON array of match criteria, ALL must match (AND): [{"column":"code","value":"attr:code","matchType":"exact"},{"column":"name","value":"Untied States","matchType":"fuzzy","threshold":0.7}]. value is a literal or "attr:<name>". Authored via the Inspector's match-parameter rows; this raw field stays the LLM-authoring vocabulary (docs/adr/0025).

ConfigFields.Label: Include expired rows
ConfigFields.Description: Off by default -- Expired rows never match unless explicitly included.

ConfigFields.Label: Stop at first match
ConfigFields.Description: Stops scanning after the first match. The output shape stays the same typed Object either way -- results just has at most one entry -- so turning this on or off never changes what a downstream Decision/binding can reference.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the typed search-result object.

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always resolve this List's current rows. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact published snapshot, unaffected by later row edits.

nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged; matches -> a typed Object attribute ({results, matched, first_match, match_count, list_id})

nodeTypes.Label: MCP: tool call
nodeTypes.Description: Calls one tool on a Configure-authored MCP server and replaces the payload with its text result (docs/SPEC.md §3.6). mcpServerId is FieldText for the same reason integration-http's requestId is -- runtime, Configure-authored data (the Inspector renders a live picker for it, RefKind, docs/adr/0009); toolName is picked from the server's live tool list in the canvas Inspector (MCPToolArgsEditor.tsx), falling back to typing the exact name when the server can't be reached.

ConfigFields.Label: MCP Server ID
ConfigFields.Description: The ID of an MCP server configured on the Configure page.

ConfigFields.Label: Tool name
ConfigFields.Description: The exact tool name, from that server's own tool list.

ConfigFields.Label: Arguments (JSON)
ConfigFields.Description: Optional JSON object of arguments to pass to the tool. Top-level string values of the form "attr:<name>" resolve to the named Attribute's typed value at run time (a number/boolean Attribute stays a JSON number/boolean, not stringified); every other value is sent as-is.

nodeTypes.Label: AI: Classify
nodeTypes.Description: Sends the running payload (plus an optional instruction) to a Configure-authored AI provider and asks it to pick exactly one of this step's own declared categories, writing the choice into a named Attribute -- a dedicated classification step (Dify's own precedent researched in docs/goals/0031-ai-node-family.md), not composed from extract-structured, since "pick one of these labels" is common enough across real workflows to deserve its own shape. Pairs with Branch: route on the written Attribute to act on the classification. The category list is this workflow's own business decision (step-local, not Configure-authored) -- two workflows classifying into different category sets is normal, not drift.

ConfigFields.Label: AI provider
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored AI provider (local Ollama or a BYO endpoint) this step calls.

ConfigFields.Label: Instruction
ConfigFields.Description: Optional guidance sent as the user message, followed by the current payload. Leave empty to classify the payload with no extra instruction.

ConfigFields.Label: Categories
ConfigFields.Description: One category per line -- the AI picks exactly one of these.

ConfigFields.Label: Write category to
ConfigFields.Description: The declared Attribute key the chosen category is written into.

nodeTypes.Output: unchanged payload -- the chosen category is written into the named Attribute below

nodeTypes.Label: AI: Completion
nodeTypes.Description: Sends a prompt (plus the running payload) to a Configure-authored AI provider -- local Ollama, or a BYO OpenAI-compatible/Anthropic endpoint -- and replaces the payload with its text completion. Composition (docs/goals/0031-ai-node-family.md): the system prompt is this step's own System prompt field; the user message is Prompt followed by the current payload (blank-line separated) when the payload is non-empty, else Prompt alone. One deterministic call per run -- never a loop or autonomous agent behavior (docs/SPEC.md §1.1's locked invariant). A local (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1) provider runs without an approval ask; any other endpoint asks by default, the same posture integration-http already has for outbound calls.

ConfigFields.Label: AI provider
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored AI provider (local Ollama or a BYO endpoint) this step calls.

ConfigFields.Label: System prompt
ConfigFields.Description: Optional system-level instruction sent ahead of the user message. Leave empty for none.

ConfigFields.Label: Prompt
ConfigFields.Description: The instruction sent as the user message, followed by the current payload (if any).

nodeTypes.Output: the AI completion text, replacing the payload

nodeTypes.Label: AI: Extract structured data
nodeTypes.Description: Sends a prompt (plus the running payload) to a Configure-authored AI provider, requests a JSON-schema-constrained structured response, and writes each declared output field into this workflow's Attributes by the same key -- the step that composes with Branch for real decisioning (docs/goals/0031-ai-node-family.md). Composition matches process-ai-completion: user content = Prompt + payload. Every declared field is required in the requested schema; a field the provider's response omits still appears in Attributes, zero-valued for its type.

ConfigFields.Label: AI provider
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored AI provider (local Ollama or a BYO endpoint) this step calls.

ConfigFields.Label: Prompt
ConfigFields.Description: The extraction instruction sent as the user message, followed by the current payload (if any).

ConfigFields.Label: Output fields
ConfigFields.Description: The typed fields this step extracts -- each becomes an Attribute of the same key, authored via the field editor below (not raw JSON).

nodeTypes.Output: unchanged payload -- the extracted typed result is written into the named Attributes below

nodeTypes.Label: Atlas: find cards
nodeTypes.Description: Searches a Kind's cards in Atlas against one or more match parameters (exact or fuzzy, AND'd together) and writes the result into Attributes. Match against "title" or any of the Kind's own field keys.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: Which Atlas card kind to search.

ConfigFields.Label: Match parameters
ConfigFields.Description: JSON array of match criteria, ALL must match (AND): [{"column":"title","value":"attr:leadName","matchType":"exact"},{"column":"status","value":"New","matchType":"exact"}]. value is a literal or "attr:<name>".

ConfigFields.Label: Stop at first match
ConfigFields.Description: Stops scanning after the first match.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the typed search-result object.

nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged; matches -> a typed Object attribute ({results, matched, first_match, match_count})

nodeTypes.Label: Process: extract HTML subtree
nodeTypes.Description: Extracts one element (by CSS selector) out of the payload's HTML, dropping everything else -- e.g. a saved page's main-content region, stripping nav/header/footer chrome before converting to Markdown. Fails the step if nothing matches (fail-safe: never silently passes the whole, unfiltered document through).

ConfigFields.Label: CSS selector
ConfigFields.Description: A CSS selector, optionally comma-separated (e.g. "#main-content, main, article") -- the first matching element (in document order) is kept.

nodeTypes.Label: Process: HTML → Markdown
nodeTypes.Description: Converts HTML into Markdown, preserving structure (headings, bold, lists).

nodeTypes.Label: Process: Inject text
nodeTypes.Description: Prepends or appends configured static text to the payload -- e.g. a fixed hint or instruction pasted alongside a workflow's real output.

ConfigFields.Label: Text to inject
ConfigFields.Description: The literal text this step adds to the payload. Left empty, this step is a no-op.

ConfigFields.Label: Placement
ConfigFields.Description: Where the text goes relative to the existing payload.

nodeTypes.Label: Process: Run receipt
nodeTypes.Description: Renders this run's own recorded evidence -- its steps so far, their guardrail verdicts, and which Mill build ran them -- as a JSON receipt, replacing the payload. Only covers steps that ran BEFORE this one, since the run is still in flight when this step executes. Compose it with an Apply step (clipboard/file write) to hand the receipt to an external agent -- there is no separate send path.
nodeTypes.Output: a JSON receipt of this run's steps so far

nodeTypes.Label: Ruleset validation
nodeTypes.Description: Validates the data flowing through this step against a set of named rules (business/data validation -- e.g. "amount below limit", "country allowed"). Every rule must pass for the payload to continue unchanged; any failing rule fails the run, naming exactly which rules failed. A rule that cannot evaluate counts as failed (fail-safe). Distinct from Decision (which routes) and from guardrail rules (which govern whether a step may execute at all).
nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged, if all rules pass

nodeTypes.Label: Atlas: create card
nodeTypes.Description: Creates a new card in Atlas of the chosen Kind. "Field values" binds the Kind's own declared fields, each a literal or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: Which Atlas card kind to create.

ConfigFields.Label: Title
ConfigFields.Description: The new card's title -- a literal or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Field values
ConfigFields.Description: JSON object mapping the Kind's field keys to a literal or attr:<name>, e.g. {"status":"New","owner":"attr:currentUser"}.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the new card's id, so a later step can reference it (e.g. to link it or update it further).

nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged; the new card's id -> the output attribute, if named

nodeTypes.Label: Atlas: link cards
nodeTypes.Description: Creates a typed relation between two existing Atlas cards. "From"/"To" are each a literal card id or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: From
ConfigFields.Description: The relation's source card -- a literal card id, or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: To
ConfigFields.Description: The relation's target card -- a literal card id, or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Relation
ConfigFields.Description: Which kind of relation this is.

ConfigFields.Label: Label (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: An optional note describing this specific relation.

nodeTypes.Label: Atlas: update card
nodeTypes.Description: Writes field values onto an existing Atlas card, resolved by "Card" (a literal card id or attr:<name> -- e.g. attr:cardId from a trigger-atlas-card event, or an earlier Atlas: find cards result). Only the fields named in "Field values" change; everything else on the card is untouched.

ConfigFields.Label: Kind
ConfigFields.Description: The card's own Kind -- names which field keys "Field values" may bind.

ConfigFields.Label: Card
ConfigFields.Description: Which card to update -- a literal card id, or attr:<name>.

ConfigFields.Label: Field values
ConfigFields.Description: JSON object mapping the Kind's field keys to a literal or attr:<name>, e.g. {"status":"Processed"}.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the updated card's id.

nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged; the updated card's id -> the output attribute, if named

nodeTypes.Label: Atlas: create from reply items
nodeTypes.Description: Creates Atlas records from an accepted clipboard reply's items: an item with a "title" becomes a card of its named kind, an item with "text" becomes a Scratchpad note. "Items" binds the attribute holding the accepted items as a JSON array.

ConfigFields.Label: Items attribute
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field carries the accepted reply items (a JSON array).

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives a summary of what was created.

nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged; a created-summary JSON -> the output attribute, if named

nodeTypes.Label: Apply: back up Mill data
nodeTypes.Description: Takes a safe snapshot of your workflow history and settings, deleting older snapshots beyond how many you keep.

ConfigFields.Label: Snapshots to keep
ConfigFields.Description: How many recent backups to keep -- older ones are deleted automatically.

nodeTypes.Label: Apply: write HTML to clipboard
nodeTypes.Description: Writes configured HTML to the clipboard.

ConfigFields.Label: HTML to write
ConfigFields.Default:
Quarterly update

Here's a quick summary, with the important bit called out.

  • Runbook actions now support global keyboard shortcuts
  • Clipboard capture preserves real structure, not flattened text
  • The UI now runs on Primer, not hand-rolled CSS
ConfigFields.Description: The HTML content this step puts on the clipboard.

nodeTypes.Label: Apply: write plain text to clipboard
nodeTypes.Description: Writes the workflow's current payload to the clipboard as plain text.

nodeTypes.Label: Apply: move file
nodeTypes.Description: Moves or renames a local file to a new location.

ConfigFields.Label: Source file
ConfigFields.Description: File to move. Leave empty to use the incoming payload, or set a path or attr: value.

ConfigFields.Label: Destination
ConfigFields.Description: Where the file goes. Tokens: {filename} {name} {ext} {date:2006-01-02} {attr:key}. End with / to keep the file's name.

ConfigFields.Label: Create missing folders
ConfigFields.Description: Creates the destination's parent folders if they don't exist yet. Off fails the step instead when a folder is missing.

ConfigFields.Label: If the destination exists
ConfigFields.Description: Fail stops the step. Suffix adds " (2)", " (3)", and so on to the file name.

nodeTypes.Label: Apply: write to file
nodeTypes.Description: Writes the payload to a local file, appending to or overwriting its existing contents.

ConfigFields.Label: File path
ConfigFields.Description: Where to write. Use an absolute path, or start with ~ for your home folder.

ConfigFields.Label: Mode
ConfigFields.Description: Append adds to the end of the file. Overwrite replaces its entire contents.

ConfigFields.Label: Create missing folders
ConfigFields.Description: Creates the file's parent folders if they don't exist yet. Off fails the step instead when a folder is missing.

ConfigFields.Label: Timestamp
ConfigFields.Description: Append mode only: "datetime" puts a date-and-time line before each entry. Ignored in overwrite mode.

nodeTypes.Label: List: apply row
nodeTypes.Description: Creates or updates a row in a Configure-authored List: if an existing row's "Key column" value matches, only the fields named in "Field values" change (everything else on that row is untouched); otherwise a new row is appended. "Field values" binds the List's own declared column keys, each a literal or attr:<name> -- the same shape apply-atlas-card-create/update use.

ConfigFields.Label: List
ConfigFields.Description: The Configure-authored List to write to.

ConfigFields.Label: Key column
ConfigFields.Description: Which column identifies a row -- an existing row whose value in this column matches gets updated; no match appends a new row.

ConfigFields.Label: Field values
ConfigFields.Description: JSON object mapping the List's column keys to a literal or attr:<name>, e.g. {"task":"attr:taskName","status":"Done"}. Must include a value for the key column.

ConfigFields.Label: Output attribute (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Which Attributes field receives the row's id.

nodeTypes.Output: payload unchanged; the row's id -> the output attribute, if named

nodeTypes.Label: Branch: route
nodeTypes.Description: Routes to one of several next steps based on a rule evaluated against this workflow's Attributes. A pure routing point -- its conditions live on its outgoing edges (SPEC.md §3.5), not here.
nodeTypes.Output: payload and Attributes unchanged; routes to the matching outgoing edge

nodeTypes.Label: Decision
nodeTypes.Description: Ends the workflow with a Configure-authored, typed terminal outcome (docs/adr/0027): an outcome category (approve/deny/manual-review/action-needed/uncategorized) plus this Decision's own typed result fields. A manual-review Decision parks the run in the Review queue first -- approve continues to the outcome, deny/timeout fails closed, same mechanism the human-review step uses. A Decision with a configured webhook fires it (the same HTTPRequest execution path integration-http uses, with the outcome's typed outputs as the body) once the outcome is computed, and -- unlike a plain Decision -- asks for approval by default, exactly like integration-http does for the identical kind of outbound call.

ConfigFields.Label: Decision
ConfigFields.Description: Which Configure-authored Decision this terminal step reaches.

ConfigFields.Label: Pin to version (optional)
ConfigFields.Description: Leave empty to always resolve this Decision's current definition. Enter a version number to pin this step to that exact published snapshot, unaffected by later edits.

import.idPresentKnownLocally: update in place through the existing chokepoint
